items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Washington Hotel, the Blue Mirror, the Ebony Plaza, then you had Bop City, the after hours spot, Jackson’s Nook after hours, another place on McAlister after hours, I don’t know what the name of it was but I went in there one night and Wes Montgomery was in there with his group.

ctx.x: Well yes, on one hand it was positive. The 49er band, they got integrated. Because the 49ers, our football team, they were playing at Keesar Stadium then. That was out in the park. And they had a forty piece band and the band became integrated. And then of course by then, by 1960, many of the clubs like the Black Hawk, they were hiring traveling bands and local bands, and many of the clubs, they hired mixed bands. In a way you know you figure — Al Forbes, our Secretary/Treasurer/Business Agent, the one that took…

lady, she had gone to Juilliard, she had played all over Europe, and she played in the symphony, so they wouldn’t let her — the probationary period. So Kurt Adler from the opera orchestra, he took her into the opera orchestra. So she played in the opera orchestra for years. And she went somewhere, I don’t know where she went, whether she went back East or whether she went over to Europe. But she was a fine tympanist. But see tympani players, that’s a high paid job in percussion because you have all the doubles.…
Well of all the people you’ve played with over the years, is there one that stands out as a terrifically interesting character?
